AppleInsider reported that Apple "just laid off an entire team dedicated to VR development," with at least 60 employees affected. Here are the details.

Apple is reportedly scaling back its Vision team

According to reliable sources cited in the report, "Apple has laid off at least 60 employees associated with the Apple Vision Group and related positions in its VR team." Apple neither confirmed nor responded to the report.

A little over a year ago, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman reported that Apple had disbanded the Vision Products Group, and Mike Rockwell, who had led the team, was reassigned to oversee the overhaul of Siri. Last May, Gurman reorganized his reporting as follows:

Gurman further noted that Apple remains committed to visionOS and its broader spatial computing vision, even as the company has lowered the priority of developing new closed-type headset devices, redirecting resources toward other AI wearables.

This news came two months ago after Justin Ryan of Spatial Insider posed a question to Steve Sinclair, Apple's senior director of visionOS product marketing, regarding reports about Apple shelving the Vision Pro and disbanding the team behind it.

Sinclair responded as follows:

Sinclair's response also echoes comments made in April by incoming CEO John Ternus. At the time, Ternus said Apple is still in the "early chapters" of spatial computing, describing the Vision Pro as a "remarkable product," and noted that use cases for the product in enterprise and healthcare continue to grow.

The most upvoted comment was posted by JustNeedItForDev

Even in today's insane cost environment, $3,700 (before sales tax) is just too much for the average user. Even power users, unless they really love AR/VR, would find it hard to justify spending that much on a device. At that price, you could almost get a pretty decent MBP (though used, and before RAMageddon hits).

Last October, the Apple Vision Pro received a hardware upgrade with the M5 chip, capable of rendering 10% more pixels, with a maximum refresh rate of 120Hz, while maintaining its $3,499 price point. Then in June last year, due to ongoing memory chip shortages, Apple raised the price to $3,699, with the price hike also affecting other products including Apple TV, iPad, Mac, and HomePod.

The AppleInsider report also comes against a larger backdrop of Apple's strategic priorities reportedly shifting, with more resources being allocated toward developing AI-powered smart glasses.

The first model is expected to be unveiled at WWDC 2027 and officially launched later that same year. The product is rumored to rely on cameras, Siri, and Visual Intelligence rather than using an AR display. Apple had originally hoped to unveil the glasses this year and officially release them in early 2027, but with growing public backlash against Meta AI glasses, the company pushed back the timeline after reassessing privacy-related concerns about the product.
